controls.title: Verified callback
controls.description: Confirm unusual requests using a previously known contact number.

controls.title: Independent approval
controls.description: Require a second authorized person to approve sensitive actions.

controls.title: Transaction limits
controls.description: Enforce payment limits that reduce the maximum fictional loss.

controls.title: Phishing-resistant authentication
controls.description: Use authentication designed to resist credential phishing.

controls.title: Message filtering
controls.description: Filter suspicious messages before users act on them.

controls.title: Awareness training
controls.description: Teach warning signs and reporting procedures.

controls.title: Source verification
controls.description: Check original trusted sources through an independent channel.

controls.title: Least privilege
controls.description: Limit the data and account privileges available to an employee.

controls.title: Login rate limiting
controls.description: Bound repeated authentication attempts on the server.

controls.title: Progressive lockout
controls.description: Use progressive delays and monitored lockouts without enabling easy denial of service.

controls.title: Unique passwords
controls.description: Avoid password reuse across services; use a password manager.

controls.title: Human code review
controls.description: Review generated code and verify its trust boundaries before release.

controls.title: Static security analysis
controls.description: Check selected risky code patterns without executing the source.

controls.title: Dependency review
controls.description: Check dependency provenance and known issues through an approved review process.

scenarios.title: AI-assisted phishing
scenarios.description: A fictional employee receives a convincing message impersonating internal support.
scenarios.rationale: The example assumes a plausible message and access to departmental information.

stages.title: Context
stages.narrative: The narrative assumes generic public company information is available.
stages.warning_sign: Unexpected familiarity is not proof of identity.
stages.intervention: Limit publicly shared organizational detail.

stages.title: Message preparation
stages.narrative: The scenario describes polished synthetic text attributed to support.
stages.warning_sign: Professional wording can still conceal a false identity.
stages.intervention: Check the request through official support channels.

stages.title: Fictional delivery
stages.narrative: A simulated message requests an account-related action.
stages.warning_sign: Unsolicited sign-in requests or unfamiliar domains.
stages.intervention: Use a known bookmark rather than the supplied link.

stages.title: Decision
stages.narrative: The fictional employee considers responding under pressure.
stages.warning_sign: Urgency and discouraging verification.
stages.intervention: Pause, verify and report.

stages.title: Potential impact
stages.narrative: If the request is trusted, account misuse may follow.
stages.warning_sign: Unexpected authentication or account activity.
stages.intervention: Use approved incident reporting and revoke compromised access.

consequences: Operations: account misuse and recovery downtime.

rules.rationale: Assume a functioning filter blocks some suspicious delivery paths.
Assume trained staff pause and verify unusual requests.
Applies to the credential-compromise objective of this scenario.
Restricted account scope limits accessible data.

scenarios.title: Executive voice deepfake
scenarios.description: A fictional accounting employee receives a payment request attributed to an executive.
scenarios.rationale: The example assumes trusted-sounding authority and substantial payment authority.

stages.title: Context
stages.narrative: The narrative assumes the executive is familiar to the employee.
stages.warning_sign: Familiarity can be imitated.
stages.intervention: Keep payment procedures independent of perceived identity.

stages.title: Voice claim
stages.narrative: The scenario describes a synthetic voice claiming executive authority.
stages.warning_sign: Voice alone does not prove identity.
stages.intervention: Verify through a previously established contact channel.

stages.title: Fictional request
stages.narrative: The simulated caller asks for an exceptional payment.
stages.warning_sign: A new beneficiary or changed payment details.
stages.intervention: Confirm beneficiary details using approved records.

stages.title: Pressure
stages.narrative: The narrative introduces urgency and a request for secrecy.
stages.warning_sign: Bypassing normal approval steps.
stages.intervention: Follow independent approval even for senior staff.

stages.title: Potential impact
stages.narrative: If authorized incorrectly, a fictional transfer may cause loss.
stages.warning_sign: Unusual payment pattern.
stages.intervention: Apply transaction limits and notify the financial response team.

consequences: Operations: payment investigation and recovery work.
Reputation: loss of confidence in financial controls.

rules.rationale: Use a trusted existing number; calling a number supplied in the request does not qualify.
Overlaps callback; the group maximum avoids double counting.
Assume the second approver independently verifies the transaction.
Assume an enforced cap materially reduces the payment exposure.
Staff are assumed to recognize pressure and follow verification.

scenarios.title: Video deepfake impersonation
scenarios.description: A fabricated executive video appears to instruct a fictional employee to disclose information.
scenarios.rationale: The example assumes convincing authority cues and access to sensitive information.

stages.title: Context
stages.narrative: The narrative assumes the target recognizes an executive.
stages.warning_sign: Recognizing a face does not authenticate a request.
stages.intervention: Define trusted channels for sensitive instructions.

stages.title: Video claim
stages.narrative: A fictional video presents an instruction attributed to the executive.
stages.warning_sign: Visual realism is not proof of authenticity.
stages.intervention: Check the original trusted source.

stages.title: Fictional delivery
stages.narrative: The scenario presents the video through an unexpected channel.
stages.warning_sign: An unverified upload or unusual account.
stages.intervention: Use an established organizational channel for verification.

stages.title: Decision
stages.narrative: The target is asked to release sensitive information.
stages.warning_sign: A request that bypasses disclosure policy.
stages.intervention: Require independent authorization.

stages.title: Potential impact
stages.narrative: Improper disclosure could affect the fictional organization.
stages.warning_sign: Unexpected public or third-party use of information.
stages.intervention: Report the incident and limit further disclosure.

consequences: Reputation: fabricated authority damages public trust.
Operations: clarification and incident response effort.

rules.rationale: Assume verification against an independent trusted source.
Overlaps source verification and is not counted twice.
An independent reviewer checks the disclosure request.
Staff understand that convincing video does not establish identity.
Reduce the information available for disclosure.

scenarios.title: AI-assisted password guessing
scenarios.description: A fictional account faces repeated password guesses; AI may help prioritize guesses, but does not bypass authentication controls.
scenarios.rationale: The teaching example assumes a guessable password and weak online attempt controls. No guesses are generated or attempted.

stages.title: Exposure
stages.narrative: A fictional login account is identified in the narrative.
stages.warning_sign: Repeated failed sign-ins.
stages.intervention: Monitor authentication events and protect account identifiers.

stages.title: Prioritization
stages.narrative: AI is described as potentially ranking likely guesses, not breaking encryption.
stages.warning_sign: Predictable or weak password choices.
stages.intervention: Use long unique passwords or passkeys.

stages.title: Repeated attempts
stages.narrative: The story describes unsuccessful login attempts without performing any.
stages.warning_sign: Bursts of failures or distributed unusual attempts.
stages.intervention: Enforce server-side rate limits and progressive delays.

stages.title: Potential compromise
stages.narrative: A guessed password could expose the fictional account.
stages.warning_sign: Unexpected successful sign-in after failures.
stages.intervention: Require strong authentication, restrict privileges and investigate.

consequences: Operations: account lockout and response work.
Reputation: loss of trust following compromise.

rules.rationale: Assume server-side limits meaningfully constrain repeated attempts.
Overlaps rate limiting; delays must avoid easy denial of service.
Assume a long, non-predictable unique password, not uniqueness alone.
A password alone is insufficient when the protected authentication path requires another resistant factor or passkey.
Limit what a compromised account can access.

scenarios.title: AI-assisted credential reuse
scenarios.description: A fictional service faces reuse of previously exposed credentials; AI may help organize data but does not make every credential valid.
scenarios.rationale: The example assumes password reuse and sensitive account data. No credential lists are loaded, generated or tested.

stages.title: Prior exposure
stages.narrative: The narrative assumes credentials were exposed at another fictional service.
stages.warning_sign: Notifications of password exposure.
stages.intervention: Reset exposed credentials and avoid reuse.

stages.title: Reuse hypothesis
stages.narrative: A hypothetical attacker expects the same password to work elsewhere.
stages.warning_sign: Shared passwords across services.
stages.intervention: Use a unique password for every service.

stages.title: Fictional login attempts
stages.narrative: The scenario describes reuse attempts without contacting a login endpoint.
stages.warning_sign: Unusual failed and successful authentication patterns.
stages.intervention: Rate-limit attempts and require strong authentication.

stages.title: Potential impact
stages.narrative: Successful reuse could expose the fictional customer account.
stages.warning_sign: New-device access or unexpected changes.
stages.intervention: Revoke suspicious sessions and follow the response process.

consequences: Finance: misuse of account capabilities where available.

rules.rationale: A unique password removes the assumed cross-service reuse path in this model; other risks remain.
Assume the additional authentication requirement cannot be satisfied with the reused password.
Limits attempts but is not assumed to stop every valid reused credential.
Overlaps repeated-attempt controls.
Restrict account data and actions.

scenarios.title: Security flaws in AI-generated code
scenarios.description: A fictional team accepts generated code containing risky input handling or unsafe library usage.
scenarios.rationale: The example assumes generated suggestions reach production without adequate review. The risk engine does not infer vulnerabilities from source.

stages.title: Code suggestion
stages.narrative: A fictional assistant proposes an implementation.
stages.warning_sign: Confident explanations without verified security assumptions.
stages.intervention: Treat generated suggestions as untrusted contributions requiring review.

stages.title: Trust boundary
stages.narrative: A snippet handles input from an untrusted source.
stages.warning_sign: Dynamic execution, shell interpolation or unsafe deserialization.
stages.intervention: Map input sources and use restricted, safe APIs.

stages.title: Review gap
stages.narrative: The hypothetical change passes without relevant checks.
stages.warning_sign: No tests covering hostile inputs or dependency provenance.
stages.intervention: Combine human review, static checks and behavior tests.

stages.title: Potential impact
stages.narrative: Unsafe code could expose the fictional application.
stages.warning_sign: Unexpected execution, data access or certificate errors ignored.
stages.intervention: Repair the root cause and apply least privilege.

consequences: Integrity: unintended code or command execution.
Operations: incident response and service disruption.

rules.rationale: Assume a knowledgeable reviewer inspects the relevant trust boundaries.
Overlaps review detection; the built-in AST module covers only four limited pattern families, not all vulnerabilities.
Assume provenance and dependency risks relevant to the change are reviewed.
Limit permissions of a deployed component.
